training_configuration.finding: The checkpoint fusion_model_v1_1.pth was strictly trained on sequences capped at 1,000 patches.

original_evaluation_configuration.finding: The published report was generated under unseeded capped execution (an instance of Protocol 3).

protocol_roles.protocol_1_training_aligned_capped_seed4: Faithful operational counterpart to original training/eval configuration. Strictly capped at 1,000 patches with fixed seed=42.
protocol_roles.protocol_2_full_uncapped_candidate: Exploratory edge deployment candidate. Leverages model's computational capacity for flexible N to evaluate complete slide evidence without tile dropping.
protocol_roles.recommendation: Preserve Protocol 1 as the training-aligned baseline while benchmarking Protocol 2 as a deployment candidate. Do not silently replace the original protocol.

protocol_1_training_aligned_capped_seed4.description: Capped at 1000 patches using deterministic torch.manual_seed(42), matching training pipeline.

protocol_2_full_uncapped_candidate.description: Full sequence evaluated without capping or tile dropping (N in [10, 3914]). Candidate deployment mode.

protocol_3_legacy_unseeded_monte_carlo.description: 10 unseeded stochastic trials matching legacy training DataLoader subsampling.

numerical_tolerances_and_determinism_gui.guideline: Bit-exact determinism cannot be assumed across different runtimes (PyTorch vs ONNX Runtime vs NNAPI). Floating-point non-associativity, SIMD vectorization, and compiler optimizations cause minor numerical divergence.

host_development_profile.context: x86_64 host developer machine (Windows 11, Intel CPU, 4 PyTorch threads)
host_development_profile.note: Peak RSS reflects batch preloading of all 66 holdout tensor pairs in memory for multi-trial evaluation.

mobile_runtime_target_expectation.note: Host development latency and memory must NOT be directly extrapolated to Android phone performance. Physical on-device profiling is required in later phases.

clinical_scope_caveat.statement: The 66-case holdout cohort is an isolated academic test partition suitable for technical verification and conversion benchmarking. It is not sufficiently powered by itself to assert generalized clinical diagnostic efficacy.
